claims: Two claim records only (request.json 5,303 B, byte-identical to the certificate's claims array, tools/prepare_test47.py:260): {reverse:false|true, input_integers:true, output_integers:true, objective:'Equal', projection:[[150,117]] resp. [[117,150]], inverse:null}. The reverse direction is claimed both ways, so the kernel proves objective equality and count/y preservation in each direction.

Each claim's payload is an enumerated unit-term vector: affine_projection maps sum(x1..x150) to the 117 target integer coordinates as 150 resp. 117 explicit [index,'1'] terms, 2,507 of the 2,650 bytes per claim; verify.py-style cardinality identity is stated as data, not as a named fact.

proof_encoding: Single 'RPA 7' text certificate, 22,149,067 B -> RPX 20,219,652 B (91.3%), two blocks: the forward interval-exchange block is 22,049,767 B (99.6%) and the reverse MenuLift block 13,607 B.

Forward block: 31 nested IntervalLift stages holding 11,761 steps (10,383 Lin, 1,829 Cases with two branch bodies each, 31 Round, 31 EqPair) plus a terminal Return of 690,362 B / 513 steps; interval payloads carry 14,260 checks in 2,729,967 B, step arrays 18,708,030 B (84.5%), i.e. the certificate is dominated by hand-expanded linear-combination text.

Generated structure per verify statistics: 31 interval lifts -> 620 continuous prefix variables, 8,370 rows, 226,562 terms; 1 menu lift -> 6 binaries, 4 rows; substitution_terms 21,653, branches 8,959, obligations 837, work 38,691,982 against default work 1e9.

Depth: depth.json records json_max_depth 126 and proof_max_depth 38; the discarded linear-search version reached logical depth 53 but container depth 186 and assembly returned status INVALID with the message recursion limit exceeded at line 1 column 5501025, at the fixed serde nesting limit 128.

Byte economics: 22,149,067 B of proof for a 64,163 B source model (~345x) and a 5,303 B contract; ~711 kB of RPA per removed column, i.e. the per-edit cost is set by how the exchange is transcribed, not by the size of the edit.
reformulation: 151 v / 13 r -> 118 v / 13 r: 31 binaries restricted to zero (each with 20 distinct retained componentwise-dominating alternatives over the 12 covering rows, non-circular by construction) and 4 binaries merged into two general integers z24_117, z25_77 in [0,2] whose column is one member's column (min y + 1e-5*sum x, c1: sum x <= 20). Nonzeros including objective 1,857 -> 1,412; all 13 rows, senses, RHS, objective sense and the x151 column/domain unchanged; objective-value-preserving, not a feasible-set bijection.
agent_manual_work: Two independent full MPS decoders over the 64,163 B source (whitespace-token and fixed-field columns 2-3, 5-12, 15-22, 25-36, 40-47, 50-61) agreeing on every row sense, coefficient, RHS, bound and integer marker, in eval cells 'Parsing complete model exactly' and 'Cross-checking parsing and failed implications'.

Exhaustive exact-rational structure discovery: 132 ordered covering-row pairs with their top-20 difference maxima and explicit counterexamples, identical binary column groups [(x24,x117),(x25,x77)], 1,374 dominance pairs, 33 columns with >=20 dominators, and the non-circularity check that each removal candidate keeps >=20 dominators outside the whole removal set ('Testing row and column structure', 'Investigating safe dominance elimination').

A hand-built exact-arithmetic pipeline: Fraction parsing, a common scale of 10^9 via lcm, and decimal output formatting dec()/fmt_num with an asserted 12-character MPS field width and a 1E+12 special case ('Writing final reformulated MPS'); the first Fraction-based smoke loop hit the 30 s eval deadline (the run's single failing tool result) and was redone in scaled integers.

Constructive exchange evidence: 24,656 feasible assignment scenarios with 13,540 verified replacement steps, all 9 aggregate states, plus the independent artifact audit verify.py (151 lines) re-checking 7,440 dominance inequalities, 132 implication counterexamples and 452 scenarios ('Completing exact constructive checks', 'Auditing final artifact independently').

Manual transcription of the certificate decision: the finding (exchange restriction plus aggregation) had to be turned into 31 interval-batch stages of a prefix-AND protocol, a Round-based zero locator, four Cases-nested swap-legality closures per stage and a reverse menu split, none of which exists as a rule.

friction: No proof-construction API: the 22 MB certificate is raw dicts, with the whole per-stage protocol written out inside a 31-iteration loop (:71-145) and split across four sibling preparer modules (1,206 lines) for expression, proof, row-fact and prefix-interval plumbing.

Representation limits are invisible until assembly: the depth-186 attempt was rejected by the importer ('recursion limit exceeded at line 1 column 5501025'), and the accepted version sits at container depth 126, only two levels below the fixed limit; representation_depths (:203) runs after the certificate exists, so the redesign cost a 4,664,035 B / 20,770-id rebuild (23.34 s -> 31.65 s preparation).

The certificate's premise is the analysis agent's private audit.json (84,703 B) read as raw dicts (:259) with bare asserts (:70-73), then re-validated by a separate 178-line script (audit/audit_normalization_47_48.py) that itself counts the 7,440 dominance inequalities; dominance/exchange data has no typed home.

The contract is enumerated rather than described: 'total selected count' is spelled out as 150 and 117 explicit unit terms (2,507 B per claim), while the only compressed part is the single index pair projection [[150,117]].

Obligation references are positional and sometimes absent: mutation receipts report code=None with 'obligation 366' or 'obligation 69' (preparation.json negative_checks), and the depth failure cites a byte column in a 17,485,032 B minified one-line file, so no stage, interval or Case can be identified without recomputing the emission order.

top_capability: BATCH_TEMPLATES - the 21.1 MB is not proof content about 33 edited columns but 31 transcriptions of one exchange protocol (11,761 steps, 14,260 checks, ~711 kB each), so a compact parametrised instantiation is what changes this case's byte and depth economics.
notes: Why 33 columns cost 21.1 MB: the kernel has no dominance/exchange rule, so the edit is certified constructively - one stage per removed column, 20 prefix-AND intervals each, every obligation spelled out as an explicit linear combination (10,383 Lin steps, 14,260 interval checks, 84.5% of bytes in step arrays). Per removed column the proof carries ~711 kB, i.e. 345x the 64,163 B model, while the caller contract stays 5,303 B; the verifier itself needs only 837 obligations, 38.7M work units and 2.54 s, so the cost is entirely in the certificate text, which is exactly what the API shape controls. A better shape changes it twice over: a template instantiated 31 times removes the repetition, and a flat instantiation also relieves the container nesting that made depth 126 of a 128 limit the binding constraint. Honest limit: compressing text does not shrink the exchange argument itself; only a first-class dominance rule would.
